title_he: לְשִׁמְךָ נוֹדֶה תּוֹדָה, אֵל חַנּוּן וְנַדִּיב
review: The hymn is Psalm 119 sung as a love for the word: 1:1–4 is Ps 119:12 with 2 Tim 3:16, 2:1–4 is Ps 119:96 nearly verbatim (לְכָל תִּכְלָה רָאִיתִי קֵץ רְחָבָה מִצְוָתְךָ מְאֹד), 3:1–4 Ps 19:8–11 (הַנֶּחֱמָדִים מִזָּהָב … וּמְתוּקִים מִדְּבַשׁ), 4:1–4 John 3:16 with Rom 10:9, 5:1–4 Ps 119:105 with Deut 8:3, and 6:1–4 Exod 13:21 with Matt 28:20.

2:3–4 אַךְ מִצְוָתְךָ רְחָבָה / רְחָבָה מִכָּל־קֵץ — the Arabic وَإِنَّمَا وَصِيَّتُك / وَاسِعَةٌ جِدًّا is 'but Your commandment is very broad'; the Hebrew quotes Ps 119:96 and repeats רְחָבָה across the couplet, because the psalm's point is the comparison (every other measure has a limit) and the repetition is what makes the stanza's turn audible.

3:3 נֶחְמָדִים מִזְּהַב־טָהוֹר — the Arabic وَأَثْمَنُ مِنَ الذَّهَب is 'pricier than gold'; the Hebrew uses Ps 19:11's הַנֶּחֱמָדִים מִזָּהָב, keeping the psalm's verb of desire rather than a commercial 'more valuable', because the stanza is about loving the word and not appraising it.

4:2 פּוֹדֶה חוֹטְאִים — the Arabic مُخَلِّصِ الْخُطَاة is a title, not a clause; the Hebrew active participle keeps it a title (the Redeemer of sinners) and does not turn it into a statement about what the word does.

6:2 בַּמִּדְבָּר הַשָּׁמֵם — the Arabic مَا دُمْنَا فِي الْقَفْر is 'while we are in the waste'; the Hebrew uses שָׁמֵם, the prophetic word for the desolated land (Lev 26:34, Jer 12:11), so the stanza's wilderness is the one Israel crossed and not a general metaphor for difficulty.
